territorial_scope.description: Applies to Minnesota-state legal entities that conduct business in Minnesota or target Minnesota residents, and preempts local government rules on processing personal data.

evidence.quote: that conduct business in Minnesota or produce products or services that are targeted to residents of Minnesota

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Minnesota's Consumer Data Privacy Act (Minn. Stat. ch. 325O) gives Minnesota consumers rights over personal data and imposes controller and processor duties on entities that do business in Minnesota or target Minnesota residents above specified consumer-count or revenue thresholds. Effective July 31, 2025, with a later date for certain postsecondary institutions.
summary.long: The Act gives Minnesota consumers rights to access, correct, delete and port personal data, and to opt out of targeted advertising, sale and certain profiling, including through opt-out preference signals. Consumers may appeal refusals. Controllers must provide a privacy notice, limit collection and retention, secure personal data, and obtain consent before processing sensitive data, and before targeted advertising or sale for consumers aged 13 to 16. Consent obtained through dark patterns is invalid. Controllers may not discriminate against consumers for exercising rights, though loyalty programs are excepted. Controllers must conduct and document data privacy and protection assessments for targeted advertising, sales, sensitive data and risky profiling. Processors must follow written contracts. The Act applies to entities doing business in Minnesota or targeting residents that meet consumer-count or revenue thresholds, and excludes government entities, Indian tribes, and many health, financial and credit-reporting regimes. Small businesses may not sell sensitive data without prior consent. The Attorney General enforces the Act after a 30-day warning letter (a cure provision expiring January 31, 2026), with civil penalties of up to $7,500 per violation. The Act creates no private right of action and preempts local laws on processing personal data. It is effective July 31, 2025, and postsecondary institutions regulated by the Office of Higher Education have until July 31, 2029.

notes: Partial record: the document contains the act title and Article 5 (Secs. 1-14, Minn. Stat. ch. 325O) only. Articles 1-4 are omitted, so title-level amendments and repeals are coded as relations without their operative text. Sec. 1 adds a new section 13.6505 to chapter 13, and its subdivision 2 refers to section 325O.08. The title mentions authorizing rulemaking, but no rulemaking provision appears in the text provided. Empty target_instrument_id means no registry id is known. Terminology varies between 'data privacy and protection assessment' and 'data protection assessment' (325O.08(h)); this is not treated as a conflict. The warning-letter step in 325O.10(a) expires January 31, 2026, as written. The title lists Laws 2023, chapter 63 both as amended (article 1) and repealed (article 7).

"Affiliate" means a legal entity that controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with another legal entity.
"Biometric data" means data generated by automatic measurements of an individual's biological characteristics
"Child" has the meaning given in United States Code, title 15, section 6501.
"Consent" means any freely given, specific, informed, and unambiguous indication of the consumer's wishes
"Consumer" means a natural person who is a Minnesota resident acting only in an individual or household context.
"Controller" means the natural or legal person who, alone or jointly with others, determines the purposes and means of the processing of personal data.

definitions.term: Decisions that produce legal or similarly significant effects concerning the consumer

evidence.quote: decisions made by the controller that result in the provision or denial by the controller of financial or lending services, housing, insurance, education enrollment or opportunity
"Dark pattern" means a user interface designed or manipulated with the substantial effect of subverting or impairing user autonomy, decision making, or choice.
"Deidentified data" means data that cannot reasonably be used to infer information about or otherwise be linked to an identified or identifiable natural person
"Genetic information" has the meaning given in section 13.386, subdivision 1.
"Identified or identifiable natural person" means a person who can be readily identified, directly or indirectly.
"Known child" means a person under circumstances where a controller has actual knowledge of, or willfully disregards, that the person is under 13 years of age.
"Personal data" means any information that is linked or reasonably linkable to an identified or identifiable natural person.
"publicly available information" means information that (1) is lawfully made available from federal, state, or local government records or widely distributed media
"Process" or "processing" means any operation or set of operations that are performed on personal data or on sets of personal data, whether or not by automated means
"Processor" means a natural or legal person who processes personal data on behalf of a controller.
"Profiling" means any form of automated processing of personal data to evaluate, analyze, or predict personal aspects
"Pseudonymous data" means personal data that cannot be attributed to a specific natural person without the use of additional information
"Sale," "sell," or "sold" means the exchange of personal data for monetary or other valuable consideration by the controller to a third party.
personal data revealing racial or ethnic origin, religious beliefs, mental or physical health condition or diagnosis, sexual orientation, or citizenship or immigration status
"Specific geolocation data" means information derived from technology, including but not limited to global positioning system level latitude and longitude coordinates
"Targeted advertising" means displaying advertisements to a consumer where the advertisement is selected based on personal data obtained or inferred from the consumer's activities over time
"Third party" means a natural or legal person, public authority, agency, or body other than the consumer, controller, processor, or an affiliate of the processor or the controller.
"Trade secret" has the meaning given in section 325C.01, subdivision 5.
a government entity, as defined by section 13.02, subdivision 7a
